questions.q: A patient has damage to the intestinal brush border but preserved pancreatic amylase secretion. Which step of carbohydrate digestion is most directly impaired?
options: Initial hydrolysis of starch in the intestinal lumen
Final hydrolysis of disaccharides to absorbable monosaccharides
Transport of glucose from the intestinal lumen into enterocytes by SGLT1
Delivery of glucose from enterocytes into portal blood
questions.explain: Pancreatic amylase produces oligosaccharides and disaccharides, but brush-border enzymes such as maltase, sucrase-isomaltase and lactase complete hydrolysis to monosaccharides. Brush-border injury therefore impairs this final digestive step.

questions.q: A patient with obstructed bile flow develops steatorrhoea despite adequate pancreatic lipase secretion. Which process is most directly impaired?
options: Emulsification and formation of mixed micelles that deliver lipid digestion products to the brush border
Hydrolysis of triglycerides by pancreatic lipase
Absorption of short-chain fatty acids directly into portal blood
questions.explain: Bile salts emulsify dietary fat and form mixed micelles that keep fatty acids and monoglycerides soluble in the intestinal lumen and deliver them to the brush border. Reduced bile delivery impairs lipid absorption and can cause steatorrhoea even when pancreatic lipase is present.

questions.q: A patient with brush-border damage has reduced absorption of glucose and galactose but relatively preserved fructose absorption. Which transporter is most likely impaired?
questions.explain: Glucose and galactose enter enterocytes apically through sodium-dependent SGLT1. Fructose uses GLUT5; monosaccharides leave basolaterally mainly through GLUT2.

open.q: Which apical transporter mediates sodium-dependent uptake of glucose and galactose?

questions.q: Which pancreatic zymogen is activated in the duodenal lumen by enteropeptidase?
questions.explain: Enteropeptidase on the duodenal brush border converts trypsinogen to trypsin. Trypsin then activates several other pancreatic zymogens.

open.q: Which pancreatic zymogen is activated by enteropeptidase?

questions.q: Most dietary dipeptides and tripeptides enter small-intestinal enterocytes across the apical membrane through which transporter?
options: PEPT1, coupled to the proton gradient
questions.explain: PEPT1 is a proton-coupled oligopeptide transporter on the apical membrane of small-intestinal enterocytes. It absorbs many dipeptides and tripeptides, which are then hydrolysed intracellularly to amino acids. Free amino acids use several distinct sodium-dependent or sodium-independent transport systems.

open.q: Which apical transporter absorbs most dietary dipeptides and tripeptides into small-intestinal enterocytes?
